answer: An identity that attests to another stakes 19% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. The beacon escrow holds each stake, the forge settlement releases it, and the glacier audit lists every transfer. A farm running 164 keys therefore pays that exposure 164 times over before it earns anything, because its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
